To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ferromagnetic behavior of HOPG can be diminished and even extinguished by annealing, that the ferromagnetically active states are located at zigzag edge sites, vacancies and related defect sites, and that the ferromagentism is correlated with localized electronic states in HOPG.
the ferromagnetic properties of highly ordered pyrolitic graphite are diminished with annealing, and that the annealed samples exhibit improved charge transport.
annealing HOPG at 2300 ° C in high vacuum can diminish and extinguish ferromagnetism and that the extinction of ferro-magnetism is accompanied by improved transport properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of annealing on the magnetism of HOPG, a system that has been proposed as a model for graphene-based magnetism.
the anneal-induced changes to the electronic properties of HOPG.
the annealing of HOPG and its impact on the ferromagnetic properties of HOPG.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ferromagnetism and the associated localized states are not intrinsic to the HOPG material but instead are correlated with defects and vacancies.
the ferromagnetic signal in HOPG is not intrinsic to the material but is due to defects and/or vacancies.
the anneal-induced extinction of ferromagnetic properties of HOPG is due to the elimination of defects and vacancies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ferromagnetic properties of pristine HOPGs are related to localized edge states.
the ferromagnetic properties of HOPG are not intrinsic but rather extrinsic and are associated with the defects and vacancies present in the as-received material.
annealing can remove defects and vacancies in HOPG and thus reduce the ferromagnetization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
annealing can significantly reduce the ferromagnetization of HOPG samples, and that this is accompanied by a decrease in the concentration of defects and vacancies.

the ferromagnetic properties of HOPG are highly sensitive to the presence of defects, and that the ferromagentic signal is diminished and eventually extinguish with the anneal-induced reduction of defects.
the ferromagnetic response of HOPG is highly sensitive to the sample’s structural and electronic properties.
